lines.text: Here's a grocery add-on. Ask for fifteen dollars of fruit: it hears fifty, asks, "are you sure?", and adds it. Say no at checkout: it places the order anyway.
In a chat window, this add-on looks fine. Out loud, it breaks. Numbers get misheard. Replies read out JSON. Lists run longer than anyone can remember. And money moves without a clear yes.
This is Hearsay: preflight checks for voice add-ons. You write what your customers say. Hearsay plays it against your server, clean and misheard, and fails the build when it would go wrong out loud.
Here's how. When someone speaks, only one step is your code: the server.
Hearsay plays the rest, straight from your test case: the words, the mishearings, and the tool call the model would make. Then it checks what your server answers.
No microphone. No model. No API keys. The same result every time, so it runs on every pull request.
Every answer is graded by the rules Amazon published for add-ons: half a second per tool, short replies, no JSON, five options at most, and no payment without naming what and how much.
Here's the real run on that add-on. One take, no cuts.
Fifty instead of fifteen, taken without reading it back. A no that placed the order anyway. Twenty errors. Exit one. The build fails.
The fixed build, same tests. The misheard fifty is refused, and the add-on says why. Zero errors.
And it guards every pull request. This change let fifty dollars of fruit skip the budget. Hearsay caught it, and the check went red. One fix, and it's green.
But wait, there's more. Hearsay is also an MCP server. Your coding agent runs it, fixes what it finds, and runs it again, until it's green.
And it can't cheat: change a locked test, and the run fails.

We measured it with coding agents. A suite alone made them stop at green, so Hearsay now shows what your suite doesn't cover. The result: zero defects left behind, and better on the rules nobody told them about.
And the price? Zero. Hearsay is open source. No keys, no account. Clone it, install it, run it.
Hearsay. Hear it before your customers do.
